items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: people like Harry Shields and Johnny Dodds, uh, were spectacularly able to anticipate the, the thinking process of the leaders with whom they played.

ctx.x: can you just explain a little more what you mean by harmony because that doesn't mean that the clarinet, for instance, plays the exact same notes as the trumpet but in harmonic relationship to the trumpet.

Well, uh, let me, let me state it this way. I would say that articulated or not that the, the New Orleans clarinet player of the pre-1915 period, uh, uh, strove to achieve precisely that. He would have considered himself the perfect clarinet player were he able to improvise note-for-note harmony with the cornet lead. Now, of course, that was a concept that, uh, by its nature is beyond the hope of, of a human performer. But it was amazing how closely some of the musicians were able to approximate this. Uh, people…
